chains.instrument: Free Legal Aid Act and annual regulation setting compensation for secondary legal aid
chains.evidence: The official MPUDT legal-instrument page inspected 2026-10-19 lists NN 142/25 as the annual secondary-legal-aid compensation regulation for 2025 and the latest annual instrument shown. The official Gazette text expressly names 2025, sets the attorney point value for 2025, and entered into force eight days after publication. The 2025 text is captured, independently compared and accepted only as a year-specific provider-remuneration source; it does not establish applicant eligibility or any 2026 rate. The Ministry 2026 work plan schedules a draft for the 2027 compensation year in Q4 2026. A targeted official-title search did not surface a 2026 regulation, but this does not prove non-publication. Record the 2026 provider-rate status as unresolved.
review_questions: Obtain a complete Official Gazette search or official Ministry confirmation of whether a 2026 annual compensation regulation was published.
Recheck the Gazette and Ministry index after the Q4 2026 work-plan window; do not treat the plan or index absence as proof of non-issuance.
Capture and compare any successor before using provider compensation figures outside the 2025 period.
Keep provider remuneration separate from applicant eligibility, court-fee waiver, reimbursement and access to legal aid.

queries: "Uredba o vrijednosti iznosa za utvrđivanje naknade za pružanje sekundarne pravne pomoći za 2026"

chains.instrument: Free Legal Aid Act NN 143/13 and 98/19; State Budget Execution Act for 2026 NN 152/25
chains.evidence: Free Legal Aid Act Article 4(15) defines the budgetary base by reference to the annual budget-execution statute; Article 14(1) uses one base per household member monthly and 60 bases for assets; Article 19(3)(b) uses half the base for full-scope aid. The 2019 amendment does not alter Articles 4(15), 14 or 19. The 2026 State Budget Execution Act Article 39(2) sets the base at EUR 441.44 and Article 72 makes the Act effective from 1 January 2026. MPUDT’s official legal-instrument index lists the Free Legal Aid Act chain as NN 143/13 and 98/19. The Ministry of Finance 2026 budget page links the execution law NN 152/25, which has been captured and accepted. A bounded exact-title Gazette query found no amending act as of 2026-10-19; recheck if later amendment evidence appears. Derived thresholds are EUR 441.44 monthly per household member, EUR 26,486.40 in total assets, and EUR 220.72 per household member for full-scope aid. These are calculated amounts. The MPUDT conditions page still displays legacy kuna figures and is not current guidance.
review_questions: Recheck for a later 2026 amendment only if an official notice or source conflict appears; the latest official Ministry page and bounded Gazette query currently support the captured NN 152/25 text.
Check current Ministry forms and practical instructions against the accepted statutory eligibility categories and formulas.
Keep all euro thresholds labelled as calculations from the statutory base and formulas, not amounts printed in the Free Legal Aid Act.
Check the next annual budget-execution act before carrying the 2026 base into 2027.

chains.instrument: Zakon o općem upravnom postupku (General Administrative Procedure Act)
chains.evidence: The official Ministry law listing identifies NN 47/09 and NN 110/21. The Ministry ZUP brochure states that the Act had been amended once, identifies NN 110/21, and gives its effective date as 1 January 2022; the Gazette amendment itself states the commencement provision. Both legal texts are separately captured and independently compared. This is a verified chain for these source records, not an official consolidated text; topic-level provision mapping remains open.
limitations: Read NN 47/09 together with NN 110/21 for current wording.
The Act supplies general procedure; immigration-specific legislation may establish lawful special rules.
Map operative Croatian provisions to EEA-family-member applications, service, deadlines, administrative silence and appeal routes before treating a topic as covered.

chains.instrument: Zakon o upravnim sporovima (Administrative Disputes Act)
chains.evidence: The official Croatian courts law lists identify the Administrative Disputes Act as NN 36/24. Its official Gazette text states that it enters into force on 1 July 2024 and repeals the prior Act and its amendments. Article 3 expressly includes challenges to decisions, conduct and failure to decide or act within the statutory period; Article 12 assigns those claims to administrative courts. This supports the operative source chain, but not a consolidated text, case-law interpretation, immigration-specific route, or a complete remedy crosswalk. The Constitutional Court decision NN 39/26 concerns ZUS Article 169(2), a transitional provision, and is tracked separately; the decision’s case-specific effect/timing remains open.
limitations: Confirm any later amendment or constitutional ruling during periodic currentness review.
Map administrative appeal exhaustion, filing deadline, interim protection, costs and EEA-family application by decision type.
Use the updated judgment record for any transition-specific question; do not infer changes to the ordinary current remedy route.

chains.instrument: Constitutional Court decision U-I-2767/2025 and U-I-2768/2025, NN 39/2026, item 485
chains.evidence: The official decision is dated 31 March 2026 and published 15 April 2026. Operative point I starts constitutional review and repeals Article 169(2) of the Administrative Disputes Act NN 36/24. The affected paragraph is a transitional rule for proceedings under the previous Act where the hearing had closed before 1 July 2024. Its application to a particular pending case and exact effective timing have not been independently assessed.
limitations: This is a narrow transitional-procedure development, not evidence of a change to ordinary current EEA residence application procedures.
Use the official decision directly; a local copy is optional.

conflicts.issue: A separate MUP page lists the Foreigners Act only through NN 40/25 and third-country procedure only through NN 102/25; it omits the later NN 55/26 and NN 116/26 listed by the current Propisi page.
conflicts.resolution: Treat the separate page as a stale index copy for the two affected instruments. Use the current Propisi page checked on 2026-10-19 as the latest-version reference and record the date boundary. A complete Gazette chain is not required; resolve a specific later text only where it changes a provision material to the issue.

conflicts.issue: Older MVEP refusal page gives €42.47 (or legacy page text gives the old tariff) and cites the Foreigners Act only through NN 151/22. The current MVEP page cites NN 40/25 and 55/26 and gives €130/USD 150.71; the current Gazette tariff NN 130/25 sets €130.
conflicts.resolution: Exclude the older page from operative procedure and retain it as a stale-page control. Use the new MVEP current page plus the current Gazette tariff for fee/deadline review. The precise application to Directive 2004/38 family-member appeals and any statutory exemption remains unresolved.

conflicts.issue: The Commissioner’s English user guide displays the Right of Access to Information Act as NN 25/13 and 85/15, omitting amendment NN 69/22 listed in the current official source chain.
conflicts.resolution: The English page remains visibly dated 2019-04-04 and cites only NN 25/13 and 85/15; the Commissioner’s current official legal-framework page lists NN 25/13, 85/15 and 69/22. The “Right to access information” section is accepted as a historical record at source-library/croatia/documents/guidance/hr-access-info-commissioner-2019-historical.md, not as current procedure or deadline guidance. Use the official Act and amendment records for current work.

conflicts.issue: The live AZOP page checked 2026-10-25 still combines a current SIS rights subsection with legacy SIS II descriptions and a VIS section that does not reflect the later revised VIS-rights provisions.
conflicts.resolution: The whole page remains excluded as a current operational guide. The static “Data subject rights” subsection for SIS was compared with the live visible page and the MUP SIS route and accepted at source-library/croatia/documents/guidance/hr-azop-sis-rights.md. The old system descriptions, obsolete 25-EU-state count, and VIS section remain excluded. MUP and MVEP pages/forms remain the current direct route references; no topic or country coverage is inferred.

conflicts.issue: The official FAQ says Croatia is not a Schengen Member State and lists Moscow/Russia/Belarus/Kazakhstan filing routes. Current MVEP visa-requirements material states the Schengen acquis has applied in Croatia since 1 January 2023.
conflicts.resolution: The official FAQ article body is accepted as a historical snapshot at source-library/croatia/documents/guidance/hr-mvep-stale-faq-historical.md. It is expressly excluded from current visa, border, fee, appeal, work and filing guidance; use current official sources and verify volatile routes live.

limitations: This verifies the authority's listed amendment chain, not that each amendment is in force on every date, has no corrigendum, or has been correctly consolidated.

The listed amendment records are version-discovery leads, not a mandatory capture queue. A human-reviewed official index or text can be used within its stated scope; inspect a specific amendment only when it may change a provision material to the issue. Local-copy extraction checks are separate.

The new administrative appeal fee and court fees were located, but applicant-category exemptions, free-legal-aid relief, the EEA-family visa application/appeal distinction and compatibility with effective-remedy requirements still need legal review.

Free Legal Aid Act amendment proposal in the ministry 2026 consultation plan is not enacted law. The latest identified compensation values are annual NN 142/25 for 2025; current-year 2026 rates require rechecking.
A targeted search did not locate a 2026 annual secondary-legal-aid compensation regulation, but absence from the inspected Ministry index or search results is not proof that none exists.

The legal-aid threshold calculations are derived from the statute’s base definition and the 2026 Budget Execution Act; the Ministry conditions page still displays pre-euro kuna amounts and should be treated as stale until corrected or replaced.
source_version_policy: This index records the latest versions listed by the responsible Croatian authorities and known publication references. It is not a consolidated-text source and does not require capturing every listed amendment. For ordinary research, use the closest government-published text within its stated date/cutoff; retrieve a specific amendment only when it may materially affect the provision in scope.

official_consolidation_discovery.finding: The current MUP Propisi page links the identified EEA and third-country base instruments and amendments as separate Narodne novine records. No integrated government-published text was identified on that index; the Central Catalogue route did not expose an accessible current consolidated text in this review. This does not prove that no official consolidation exists elsewhere.
official_consolidation_discovery.review_question: Can human review locate an official integrated current text on these government portals, and verify its authority, language, displayed version/cutoff and any informational caveat?
official_consolidation_discovery.effect: The current MUP index and its linked official texts remain usable within their listed chains and cutoffs. The optional portal review does not block source use or other coverage work.
